messages:
alex: heads-up — enterprise customer (acct: acme-corp) is hitting a hard 400 on tool calls. they pass a tool call payload and get `Malformed tool arguments` back. they say it worked in prod yesterday and started failing after a client-side patch.

alex: payload they send (copied from their client):
```json
{
  'tool_name': 'extract_entities',
  'args': {
    'text': 'Invoice #1234\nAmount: $1,200.00',
    'options': {
      'locale': 'en-US',
    },
  },
}
```

alex: note the single quotes and trailing commas — obvious suspects, but they insist their client serializes with JSON.stringify in other places.

maria: can we repro locally with the same raw body? ask for the exact curl they used and the Content-Type header.

alex: they sent this curl: 
```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/toolcall" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary $'{\'\''tool_name'\'\'':'\'\''extract_entities'\'\'','\'\''args'\'\'':{\'\''text'\'\'':'\'\''Invoice #1234\\nAmount: $1,200.00'\'\'','\'\''options'\'\'':{\'\''locale'\'\'':'\'\''en-US'\'\''},,}'
```

alex: server response: 
```json
{
  "error": "Malformed tool arguments",
  "code": 400,
  "details": "JSON parse error at column 14: unexpected token '\''"
}
```

gina: thanks. looks like the client is shell-escaping single quotes into the binary payload (the $'...' form). that turns the JSON into an invalid string for our parser. two remediation paths: 1) ask client to send valid RFC-8259 JSON (double quotes, no trailing commas) or 2) make our parser return a better pointer + hint.

support-esc: customer is blocked — their ingestion pipeline fails. they want a production-safe workaround ASAP. they can't change the client quickly (third-party integrator).

eng-ryan: quick checks — we currently run a strict JSON parse for tool args and then schema-validate against the tool's arg schema. if parse fails we return 400 with generic "Malformed tool arguments". we can add heuristics to detect common issues (single quotes, trailing commas, control sequences) and return a more targeted error or warning.

eng-ryan: can you repro locally with their exact curl? if so I can prototype a tolerant parser that attempts to normalize single->double quotes and strips trailing commas, but we'd treat that as a non-production bandaid unless customer explicitly opts in.

alex: repro steps I ran: used their curl and captured request body. our raw receive shows backslashes and literal single quotes (so the client did shell interpolation). when I re-sent with a properly-escaped JSON (double quotes, no trailing commas) it worked.

alex: good repro command (what I ran):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/toolcall" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"tool_name":"extract_entities","args":{"text":"Invoice #1234\\nAmount: $1,200.00","options":{"locale":"en-US"}}}'
```

maria: perfect. next steps? customer needs an immediate workaround they can apply client-side without a full release. any ideas?

gina: three options to suggest to the integrator: 1) wrap the payload in a here-doc to avoid shell escaping, e.g. `--data-binary @- <<'EOF'` 2) base64-encode the JSON and send in a wrapper field (we can accept and decode server-side if they want) 3) change the Content-Type to `text/plain` and send the raw string — not ideal.

support-esc: customer prefers minimal code changes. they asked if we can accept `text/plain` temporarily. ops/security ok?

sre-bot: note: request-id=req_0a1b2c3d timestamp=2026-11-07T14:52:31Z routed to region=us-west-2. raw-body size=512 bytes. logged under session=acme-3312.

eng-ryan: we can add a short-term server-side tolerant path behind a feature flag: if a new header `X-Allow-quirky-json: true` is present we'll attempt to normalize common shell-escaped single-quote JSON and remove trailing commas before parsing. default remains strict. implementing this will take ~1-2 dev days including tests.

maria: that sounds reasonable. outline to customer: 1) immediate workaround using a here-doc example (gina's suggestion) 2) short-term: we can enable the tolerant parser for their API key behind a feature flag while they fix the integrator 3) mid-term: improve error message to include pointer and hint about single quotes/trailing commas.

alex: sending the here-doc example back to customer (copied):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/toolcall" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @- <<'EOF'\n{"tool_name":"extract_entities","args":{"text":"Invoice #1234\\nAmount: $1,200.00","options":{"locale":"en-US"}}}\nEOF
```

support-esc: customer replied — can you enable the flag for api-key `acct_Acme_Prod`? they said they can roll their fix in 48 hours.

eng-ryan: I'll create a feature flag and a quick endpoint switch. tagging @eng-ryan for the deploy. I'll also add an internal todo to improve our parse error message to return the offending character/pointer and a short hint (e.g., "did you mean double quotes? trailing comma?").

gina: note for postmortem: common integrations still use shell expansion in CI scripts; we should add a short blurb in docs about safe curl usage and a troubleshooting snippet.

maria: +1 to docs. also add an eval that runs a few invalid-tool-args examples to ensure error messages are clear.

support-esc: customer is unblocked after we enabled the flag. they gave :thumbsup: and said they'll patch the integrator. closing once PR for feature-flag lands.

eng-ryan: I'll follow-up with a small change list and PR link when ready.

alex: thanks team — leaving thread here. will update with PR and docs link.
